title: Anemic DTOs Used as Domain Objects
pattern: Using raw Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) as the primary objects inside core business logic or UI rendering, instead of converting them to proper domain models.
why_bad: It leaks serialization and persistence formats directly into presentation or calculation layers. Changes to database serialization libraries or fields break presentation layers immediately, causing tight horizontal coupling.
detection: DTOs or JSON/SQL serialization structs crossing deep into the UI, calculation, or validation layers of an application.
counterexample: Very simple, database-driven administrative CRUD panels with zero business logic or validation.
fix: Keep DTOs strictly at the serialization boundaries, and immediately map them to rich, behavioral domain models once they cross into application logic.
source: Martin Fowler, *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture* (2002), Chapter 15 ("Data Transfer Object").
